title: Cost Optimization Experiments: Gating & Measurement Framework
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a repeatable gating and measurement framework for cost-optimization experiments across batching, prefix/KV caching, and quantization. The framework will standardize hypotheses, metrics, guardrails, and rollout gates so PMs and Eng can run safe, comparable experiments that target unit-cost reduction without degrading latency or quality. This initiative focuses on operationalizing experiments (templates, dashboards, and automated rollouts/rollbacks) rather than model research.
objective: Enable a predictable experimentation workflow that reduces per-token cost by 10%+ on target workloads while keeping end-to-end latency SLOs and quality thresholds intact.
okrs: O1: Deliver framework and experiment templates enabling 30 engineering experiments per quarter
KR1: 10% average unit-cost reduction on 3 pilot workloads within 3 months
KR2: 0% net customer-facing quality regressions (as measured by PRF on eval sets)
KR3: Automated rollback and alerting for all experiments with defined gates
acceptance_criteria: Experiment template (batching/caching/quant) documented and available in Console as a wizard
Dashboards show per-experiment unit cost, latency P50/P95, and quality deltas vs baseline
Automated gates for canary -> ramp -> full rollout based on metric thresholds are implemented
Runbooks for rollback and customer communication are published
Two pilot experiments completed (one batching, one quantization) with learnings captured

decisions: Use 'unit_cost_per_100k_tokens' as canonical cost metric for cross-experiment comparability
Canary thresholds: require cost reduction >= 3% and no more than 2% increase in latency P95 to proceed to ramp
Quality guardrail: any experiment with >1% drop in MDF (model-defined F1/PRF) triggers immediate rollback
All experiments must include a minimum 48-hour canary period with real traffic to detect diurnal effects
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Upstream changes (e.g., model version) can confound experiment signals. Mitigation: require model pinning for experiment cohorts or label and exclude traffic from model rollouts.
Risk: Cost metrics noisy on low-traffic canaries. Mitigation: enforce minimum sample sizes or synthetic load for statistical power.
Risk: Quantization could introduce subtle semantic regressions. Mitigation: add targeted eval suites and user-facing shadow routing before ramp.
rollout_plan: Step 0: Create experiment in Console using template. Select pilot workload, model version, and baseline window.
Step 1: Canary (1% traffic) for 48 hours; metrics evaluated automatically by pipeline
Step 2: Ramp (10% -> 50%) conditioned on gates at each step (cost, latency, quality)
Step 3: Full rollout after 7 days stable metrics and post-rollout monitoring enabled
Rollback: Automatic rollback trigger if any gate threshold breached during ramp or full rollout
implementation_notes: Observability: add experiment tagging to token-level traces and cost attribution so dashboards can break down by experiment id
Runtime: batching changes will require backward-compatible API flags and a toggled kernel path to allow fast rollback
Quantization: provide bit-width metadata and fallbacks to non-quantized variant if quality drops detected
Infra: schedule synthetic load generator for low-traffic pilots to reach power thresholds
